newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INSIGHT - NZ dlr softens in run-up to key data.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - NZ dlr softens in run-up to key data.

text.p: *DAY'S RANGE * SUPPORT * RESTNCE * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
* NZ dollar opens weaker in preparation for soft CPI data
* Vulnerable Australian dollar not helping sentiment
* Volumes thin ahead of CPI, buyers sparse
The New Zealand dollar opened weaker on Tuesday at the start of what dealers said could be a dramatic session.

Key June quarter inflation data is due out at 10.45 a.m. (2245 GMT). Dealers said if the number came in low as expected, the already heavy dollar would encounter selling to the degree that might force the central bank to speak up in protest.

The Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) on Friday warned markets they had eased conditions too far, but response to the statement was muted. Monetary conditions are now as loose as they were then, as interest rates have not risen far enough to compensate for the lower kiwi dollar.
By 9.00 a.m. the monetary conditions index was at 754.90, which was 70 basis points (in interest rate terms) below the RBNZ's desired level and 20 pips outside its comfort zone.
The kiwi opened at US$0.6660/65, down from 0.6668/75 at Monday's close. By 9.00 a.m. it had slipped further to 0.6655/62, in very thin trade.
"There's nobody really too keen to take positions, especially buy positions, ahead of this CPI number," a Wellington dealer said.
"It's still very heavily offered at the moment, and it's going to need a strong number this morning to turn that around."
The currency, which encountered selling out of London and New York after the local close, traded a 0.6651-77 range overnight.
Dealers said they would not be surprised to see the kiwi test 0.6620 on a knee-jerk reaction to weak inflation news.
The Reserve Bank will calculate core inflation shortly after the release of headline inflation data from Statistics New Zealand at 10.45 a.m.

The RBNZ has forecast underlying inflation at 0.3 percent in the June quarter. Economists polled by Reuters on average forecast core inflation at 0.33 percent in the June quarter for an annual rise of 1.5 percent.

The headline CPI number, which includes government charges, changes in interest rates charges and one-offs, is forecast by economists to come out at 0.14 percent for the quarter and 1.13 percent for the year.
Dealers expected a tight 0.6650-65 range ahead of the data.
In the debt market, bank bills rallied a couple of pips at the open, and the overnight cash rate rose to eight percent from 7.60 at Monday's close.
